page: Vultr voc-s-24c-192gb-3840s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The system features 24 virtual CPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not contain any GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong CPU performance, with both stress-ng single-core and multi-core metrics placing in the top 25%. PassMark CPU and physics testing also rank in the top 25%, indicating robust computational capabilities for integer and physics simulations. Memory performance is mixed; while small-block cached read bandwidth is average, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths reach top-tier levels in the top 10%. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput consistently fall within the middle 50% of tested systems.

A primary architectural tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce resource contention compared to dedicated-core instances. However, the high density of 192.0 GB of RAM and 3840 GB of NVMe SSD storage relative to the virtual core count offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads that do not require continuous, dedicated CPU execution. This hardware profile is well-suited for large-scale databases, memory-cached applications, data indexing, and general-purpose web serving.
description: Vultr voc-s-24c-192gb-3840s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 24 vCPUs, 192.0 GB of RAM, and 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance utilizes a shared CPU allocation model. Benchmark results show strong CPU performance, with stress-ng and PassMark scores placing in the top 25%. Uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidths reach top-tier levels in the top 10%, while database operations and static web serving throughput remain in the middle 50%. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core and substantial local NVMe storage make this server highly efficient for memory-intensive workloads, database hosting, and caching layers, despite the potential performance variability associated with its shared CPU resource model.
